reason: Confirmed by running the code. In tools/runtime_ledger.py the EXP_RULES are checked in order and the first match wins (family_of, l.158-166). The rule exp8\d[a-z]* -> safetail sits at l.81, and only exp79a* has an explicit safetail_ci rule. Running family_of(exp_token(name)) gives: exp83a_k2cap12fc2_ci, biohub-exp83c-..., exp83d_... -> 'safetail' (wrong). exp82a/b, exp84a, exp80a, exp81 -> safetail (right). Under safetail the deadline is 9.5 h and the insertion gate is 8.0 h. A CI stack at its modelled L of ~9.7-10.5 h (non-CI K2 L_hi 7.04-7.81 h + CI 2.2-3 h; no CI file has scored yet) would print R5(a) NO/UNPROVEN and 'gate MAY have fired', instead of ADMIT and 'did NOT fire' under safetail_ci (10.75 h / 10.2 h, CONTEXT l.3134-3137). All seven exp83a-g scratch builds carry coordinject, so exp83[a-z]* -> safetail_ci has no false positives. Limits: this is tooling hygiene, with no LB or private value of its own. The ledger is report-only and --family overrides already work, so the harm is a misread finals/W card, not a wrong submission. Still worth the ~5 min, because W2b/W3 reads of CI lever state ('v' -> '?') come from this card overnight.
fix: In EXP_RULES, insert (r"exp83[a-z]*", "safetail_ci") above the (r"exp8\d[a-z]*", "safetail") line, with a comment citing R21 CI stacks. In tests/test_runtime_ledger.py, assert family_of('1', t, {}) == 'safetail_ci' for exp83a, exp83c, exp83d, exp83g and for exp_token('exp83c_k2cap6_secn2a_ci'). Assert 'safetail' for exp82a, exp82b, exp82c, exp84a, exp80a, exp81, and keep exp79a -> safetail_ci. Run pytest (24 -> 25+ pass). Optionally add the 10.75 h CI family to the ledger header R5(a) sentence. Tooling only: no kernel is touched, so byte-identity and fail-soft are not affected. Do it before the first exp83* dummy or submit; until then pass --family <ref>=safetail_ci.
realistic_gain: 0 LB directly. It prevents a misread of CI-stack admission and gate state on the finals/W cards (an eligible CI file coded NO or 'v' and dropped). Cost ~5 min, zero risk.
